items.title: Mirror of a classical knot
items.statement: Fix the orientation-reversing involution $r:S^3\to S^3$ given by reflection across a fixed equatorial two-sphere containing a chosen standard unknot $U$. For a smooth knot $K\subset S^3$, its mirror is $\overline K:=r(K)$, with the orientation transported by $r$. A diagram of the mirror can be obtained by keeping the projected shadow fixed and interchanging the over- and under-crossing data at every crossing; equivalently, one may reflect the planar shadow while retaining the crossing data. These are alternative mirror conventions, not operations to perform together. Since $r^2=\mathrm{id}$ and $r(U)=U$, mirroring twice returns $K$, and $K$ is the unknot exactly when $\overline K$ is.

references.title: P. B. Kronheimer and T. S. Mrowka, Khovanov homology is an unknot-detector, §§1.1 and 8.6–8.7

items.title: Essential torus curves with the same primitive class are isotopic
items.statement: Let $T=\mathbb R^2/\mathbb Z^2$ be oriented by $dx\wedge dy$, and identify $H_1(T;\mathbb Z)$ with $\mathbb Z^2$ in the standard basis, so the algebraic intersection of classes $v,w$ is $\det(v,w)$. Let $\gamma_0,\gamma_1\subset T$ be smooth embedded circles that are not null-homotopic. Orient them so that their homology classes agree, and suppose their common class $v\in H_1(T;\mathbb Z)$ is primitive, meaning it is not an integer multiple $m u$ with $|m|>1$. Then $\gamma_0$ and $\gamma_1$ are isotopic through embedded circles in $T$.

items.title: The normal-boundary Hodge estimate on four-dimensional balls

references.title: Terence Tao and Gang Tian, A singularity removal theorem for Yang–Mills fields in higher dimensions, Proposition 3.5 and §9
Katrin Wehrheim, Uhlenbeck Compactness, public introduction, Theorem D

items.statement:
Assume full AC. Let $V$ be a fixed finite-dimensional real inner-product space, $2\le p<\infty$, let $r>0$, and put $B_r=B_r(0)\subset\mathbb R^4$. Let $Y_p(B_r;V)$ be the $W^{1,p}$ closure of smooth $V$-valued one-forms on the closed ball satisfying $a(\nu)=0$ on the sphere. Write $d^*a=-\sum_i\partial_i a_i$ and $(da)_{ij}=\partial_i a_j-\partial_j a_i$ for $i<j$. There is $C_{p,V}$ independent of $r$ such that every $a\in Y_p(B_r;V)$ satisfies
$$r^{-1}\|a\|_p+\|\nabla a\|_p\le C_{p,V}\bigl(\|da\|_p+\|d^*a\|_p\bigr).$$
Every such $a$ satisfies the zero-normal integration identity $\int\langle a,d\phi\rangle=\int\langle d^*a,\phi\rangle$ for smooth $\phi$ on the closed ball. If $da=d^*a=0$, then $a=0$.

For $V=\mathfrak{su}(2)$ with the Frobenius norm and $2\le p<4$, there exist $\rho_p>0$ and $C_p$ independent of $r$ such that, whenever $a\in Y_p$ satisfies $d^*a=0$ and $\|a\|_4\le\rho_p$, its curvature $F_a=da+a\wedge a$, $(a\wedge a)_{ij}=[a_i,a_j]$, satisfies
$$r^{-1}\|a\|_p+\|\nabla a\|_p\le C_p\|F_a\|_p.$$
All norms here are Euclidean coefficient norms; the class $Y_p$ states precisely the boundary approximation hypothesis.

items.title: A strong L2 Neumann inverse on four-dimensional balls

references.title: Sheldon Axler and Peter J. Shin, The Neumann problem on ellipsoids, Proposition 2.1, Theorem 2.2, Lemma 2.3 and Theorem 2.4, pp.263–268
Terence Tao and Gang Tian, A singularity removal theorem for Yang–Mills fields in higher dimensions, Proposition 3.6

items.statement:
Assume full AC. Let $V$ be a fixed finite-dimensional real inner-product space, let $r>0$, and write $B_r=B_r(0)\subset\mathbb R^4$. For each $f\in L^2(B_r;V)$ with $\int_{B_r}f=0$ there exists a unique $u\in W^{2,2}(B_r;V)$ with $\int_{B_r}u=0$ satisfying the Neumann problem in the weak form
$$\int_{B_r}\langle\nabla u,\nabla v\rangle=\int_{B_r}\langle f,v\rangle\qquad\bigl(v\in W^{1,2}(B_r;V)\bigr).$$
Thus $-\Delta u=f$ distributionally, and the zero-normal boundary condition is included in the displayed all-test-function identity. The inverse $f\mapsto u$ is linear and obeys
$$\|D^2u\|_2\le\|f\|_2,\qquad r^{-2}\|u\|_2+r^{-1}\|\nabla u\|_2+\|D^2u\|_2\le C\|f\|_2,$$
with $C$ independent of $r$ and $f$. The Hessian norm is the Euclidean norm on all ordered second derivatives. If $f$ is the restriction of a polynomial and has mean zero, then $u$ is the restriction of a polynomial with classical $\partial_\nu u=0$ on $\partial B_r$.

If a fixed finite $\Gamma\le O(4)$ and an orthogonal representation $\sigma:\Gamma\to O(V)$ satisfy $f(\gamma x)=\sigma(\gamma)f(x)$ almost everywhere, the unique solution satisfies $u(\gamma x)=\sigma(\gamma)u(x)$ almost everywhere. This includes $V=\mathfrak{su}(2)$ with its Frobenius norm and a prescribed action by orthogonal Lie-algebra automorphisms.

The compatibility $\int f=0$ is necessary. This is a linear $L^2$ boundary-solvability result; higher-$L^p$ Neumann estimates and nonlinear Coulomb-gauge existence are separate assertions.

items.title: A strong Lp Neumann inverse on four-dimensional balls

references.title: Terence Tao and Gang Tian, A singularity removal theorem for Yang–Mills fields in higher dimensions, Proposition 3.6 and §9

items.statement:
Assume full AC. Derivative tensors carry their Euclidean norms, and Sobolev norms are sums of the resulting $L^p$ norms. Fix a finite-dimensional real inner-product space $V$, $2\le p<\infty$, and $r>0$. Every $f\in L^p(B_r(0);V)$ with zero volume mean has a unique mean-zero $u\in W^{2,p}(B_r;V)$ satisfying
$$\int_{B_r}\langle\nabla u,\nabla v\rangle=\int_{B_r}\langle f,v\rangle\qquad(v\in W^{1,2}(B_r;V)).$$
The inverse is linear and obeys
$$r^{-2}\|u\|_p+r^{-1}\|\nabla u\|_p+\|D^2u\|_p\le C_{p,V}\|f\|_p,$$
with $C_{p,V}$ independent of $r$ and $f$. Its solution is the $W^{2,p}$ limit of mean-zero polynomial solutions with classical zero normal derivative. In particular it belongs to the $W^{2,p}$ closure of smooth zero-normal-derivative functions on the closed ball.

On $B_1$, let $X_p$ be the $W^{2,p}$ closure of the $V$-valued polynomials with zero normal derivative on the sphere, and let $X_p^0$ be its mean-zero subspace. Then $-\Delta:X_p^0\to L^p_0(B_1;V)$ is a bounded bijection with the above inverse. Here $L^p_0$ denotes the zero-mean subspace; $X_p^0$ is complete for the equivalent norm $\|u\|_{X_p^0}=\|\Delta u\|_p$. A prescribed finite orthogonal equivariance of $f$ is preserved by the inverse, as in the $L^2$ case. No endpoint $p=\infty$ or nonlinear gauge existence is asserted.

items.title: Singular instanton knot and sutured closure data
items.statement:
Assume full AC for the instanton constructions. Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth knot with a marked point $x$ and a preferred nonzero normal vector $v$ at $x$. Choose a small disk $D$ normal to $K$ at $x$, let $L=\partial D$, and let $\omega$ be the radius of $D$ from $x$ to a point of $L$. Then $K^\natural:=K\cup L$ is the based earring link. Choose disjoint closed tubular neighborhoods $N(K)$ and $N(L)$ of its two components, set $X=S^3\setminus\operatorname{int}(N(K)\cup N(L))$, and truncate the endpoints of $\omega$ at $\partial X$ to obtain $[\omega]\in H_1(X,\partial X;\mathbb Z/2)$.

Here $PU(2)=U(2)/U(1)\cong SO(3)$; a principal $PU(2)$ bundle $P\to X$ is equivalently an oriented real 3-plane bundle, and $w_2(P)\in H^2(X;\mathbb Z/2)$ denotes its second Stiefel–Whitney class. Poincaré–Lefschetz duality for the oriented compact 3-manifold $X$ with boundary is the isomorphism $PD:H_1(X,\partial X;\mathbb Z/2)\to H^2(X;\mathbb Z/2)$. Include a bundle $P$ with $w_2(P)=PD([\omega])$ in the singular bundle data.

In a local meridional angular coordinate $\theta$, an $SU(2)$ lift of the singular connection has the standard model $A_0+\frac14\begin{pmatrix}i&0\\0&-i\end{pmatrix}d\theta$, where $A_0$ is smooth in an $O(2)$ reduction. Parallel transport (holonomy) around either meridian is conjugate in $SU(2)$ to $\operatorname{diag}(i,-i)$; its image has order two in $PU(2)$. Define $I^\natural(K;\mathbb Z)$ to be the singular instanton Floer homology $I^\omega(S^3,K^\natural;P)$ associated to these data by Analytic foundations for the singular instanton knot complex, which supplies its analytic complex and independence of auxiliary choices under full AC. This does not assert sutured closure independence or a distinguished canonical class.

For the sutured version, let $E_K$ be the compact knot exterior and put two oppositely oriented meridional sutures $\gamma$ on its boundary torus. Choose a connected oriented annulus $T$, attach $[-1,1]\times T$ along the annular sutured region, and glue the two resulting boundary surfaces by an orientation-compatible diffeomorphism fixing a chosen point from $T$. The result is a closed oriented 3-manifold $\bar Y$ with a distinguished torus $\bar R$; the fixed point determines a standard circle meeting $\bar R$ once. Choose a line bundle $w\to\bar Y$ whose first Chern class is Poincaré dual to that circle, so $\langle c_1(w),[\bar R]\rangle$ is odd. Let $I_*(\bar Y,w;\mathbb Q)$ denote the closed instanton Floer group with rational coefficients, using the admissible fixed-determinant theory in the external input below. For a homology class $z$ of dimension $0$ or $2$ in $\bar Y$, let $\mu(z)$ denote the standard instanton Floer operator associated to $z$; the point and surface operators commute and have degrees $4$ and $-2$, respectively. If $y\in\bar R$, define the closure group $KHI_{\bar Y,\bar R,w}(K;\mathbb Q)$ by
$$KHI_{\bar Y,\bar R,w}(K;\mathbb Q):=\{a\in I_*(\bar Y,w;\mathbb Q):\mu(\bar R)^N a=0\text{ for some }N\ge1,\ \mu(y)a=2a\}.$$
This uses the generalized $0$-eigenspace of the surface operator and the ordinary $+2$-eigenspace of the point operator. For this admissible torus closure it equals the simultaneous ordinary $(0,2)$ eigenspace, by the extreme-surface simplicity input stated below; no global diagonalizability of either operator is assumed. The closure group is considered up to isomorphism, with independence of these auxiliary choices supplied by the external input below and the stated well-definedness justifier; no canonical vector or preferred basis is part of this definition.

items.title: A Neumann Coulomb-gauge correction by contraction

references.title: Terence Tao and Gang Tian, A singularity removal theorem for Yang–Mills fields in higher dimensions, Proposition 9.2, Step 3, pp.38–39

items.statement:
Assume full AC and work on the closed Euclidean unit ball in four dimensions. Use sums of $L^p$ norms of Euclidean ordered derivative tensors for Sobolev norms; these are equivalent to the cited scalar Sobolev norms and invariant under orthogonal coordinate changes. Let $X$ be the mean-zero $W^{2,3}$ closure of $\mathfrak{su}(2)$-valued polynomials with zero normal derivative on the sphere. Let $Y$ be the $W^{1,3}$ closure of smooth $\mathfrak{su}(2)$-valued one-forms with zero normal component on the sphere. Let $\mathcal G_N$ be the $W^{2,3}$ closure of smooth maps to $SU(2)$ with zero normal derivative on the sphere.

There exist fixed positive constants $\rho,\eta,\delta,C$ such that, if $a\in Y$ satisfies $d^*a=0$, $\|a\|_4\le\rho$, and $\lambda\in Y$ satisfies $\|\lambda\|_{W^{1,3}}\le\delta$, there exists $u\in X$, unique among $\|u\|_{W^{2,3}}\le\eta$, such that $h=e^u\in\mathcal G_N$ and
$$b=h^{-1}dh+h^{-1}(a+\lambda)h\in Y,\qquad d^*b=0.$$
Moreover
$$\|u\|_{W^{2,3}}\le C\|\lambda\|_{W^{1,3}},\qquad \|b-a\|_{W^{1,3}}\le C(1+\|a\|_{W^{1,3}})\|\lambda\|_{W^{1,3}}.$$
All constants are independent of the higher norm of $a$.

Given a finite $\Gamma\le O(4)$ and an action $\tau$ of $\Gamma$ on $SU(2)$ by constant unitary conjugations, suppose $\gamma^*a=d\tau_\gamma(a)$ and $\gamma^*\lambda=d\tau_\gamma(\lambda)$. Then $u(\gamma x)=d\tau_\gamma(u(x))$ and $h(\gamma x)=\tau_\gamma(h(x))$. A representation into $PU(2)$ supplies such a conjugation action; no lift of that representation to $SU(2)$ is required.

items.title: Instanton knot homology and its canonical isomorphism class
items.statement:
Assume full AC. For a based smooth knot $K\subset S^3$ with the earring and admissible singular-bundle data above, let $C^
atural(K;\mathbb Z)$ be the integral singular-instanton cochain complex: its generators are regular critical points of the perturbed Chern–Simons functional on the corresponding singular configuration space, and its degree-one differential counts oriented zero-dimensional moduli spaces of trajectories for the perturbed singular anti-self-dual equation. Here finite energy is the flow energy $2\int_{\mathbb R}\|\partial_tB\|_2^2dt$ in temporal gauge, equivalently the perturbed topological energy of the relative trajectory class, rather than unrenormalized curvature energy over the infinite cylinder. The grading is relative modulo four, and the differential has degree one. Define $I^
atural(K;\mathbb Z):=H^*(C^
atural(K;\mathbb Z))$ using the analytic construction and independence of choices established in Analytic foundations for the singular instanton knot complex. Write $I^
atural(K;\mathbb Q):=I^
atural(K;\mathbb Z)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb Q$. The invariant class specified here is the isomorphism class of this group with its relative grading; the continuation identifications retain the declared overall sign ambiguity.

items.statement: Assume countable choice. Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth knot with a chosen closed tubular neighborhood $N(K)$, and let $E_K=S^3\setminus\operatorname{int}N(K)$. Every smoothly embedded two-sphere in the interior of $E_K$ bounds a smoothly embedded closed three-ball contained in $E_K$.

items.statement:
Assume full AC, using Sobolev norms formed from the $L^p$ norms of Euclidean ordered derivative tensors. There exist constants $\varepsilon,C,C_3>0$ with the following property. Let $A$ be a smooth $\mathfrak{su}(2)$-valued one-form on the closed Euclidean ball $B_r(0)\subset\mathbb R^4$, with Frobenius target norm and curvature $F_A=dA+A\wedge A$. If $\|F_A\|_{L^2(B_r)}\le\varepsilon$, then there exists $g:B_r\to SU(2)$ belonging to $W^{2,p}$ for every finite $p\ge2$ such that
$$a=A^g=g^{-1}dg+g^{-1}Ag,\qquad d^*a=0,$$
and $a$ belongs to the $W^{1,3}$ closure $Y_3$ of smooth one-forms with zero normal component on the sphere. In particular the normal condition is valid in the weak integration identity. The form $a$ belongs to every $W^{1,p}$ with finite $p\ge2$ and satisfies
$$r^{-1}\|a\|_2+\|\nabla a\|_2+\|a\|_4\le C\|F_A\|_2,\qquad r^{-1}\|a\|_3+\|\nabla a\|_3\le C_3\|F_A\|_3.$$
The constants are independent of $r$ and $A$; no uniform bound on the gauge's higher norms in terms of the critical curvature norm alone is asserted.

If a fixed finite $\Gamma\le O(4)$ acts on the ball and $\tau$ is an action of $\Gamma$ on $SU(2)$ by constant unitary conjugations, assume $\gamma^*A=d\tau_\gamma(A)$. Then $g$ may be chosen with $g(\gamma x)=\tau_\gamma(g(x))$. This includes prescribed conjugation actions coming from $PU(2)$ representations, without choosing a lift to an $SU(2)$ representation.

For a finite collection of balls with smooth local connection forms $A_i$ and given smooth $SU(2)$ transition maps $t_{ij}$ satisfying $A_j=A_i^{t_{ij}}$ and $t_{ij}t_{jk}=t_{ik}$, apply the construction on each ball where its curvature bound holds. The transformed maps $h_{ij}=g_i^{-1}t_{ij}g_j$ are continuous $W^{2,3}_{\mathrm{loc}}$ transition maps on the overlaps, satisfy the cocycle identities pointwise, and identify the transformed connection forms by $a_j=a_i^{h_{ij}}$.

items.title: Analytic foundations for the singular instanton knot complex
items.statement: Assume full AC and fix a smooth based knot $K\subset S^3$ with the earring and admissible singular bundle data of the preceding definitions. For regular perturbation data, the perturbed Chern–Simons critical points and finite-energy singular anti-self-dual trajectories define a finite free cochain complex $C^\natural(K;\mathbb Z)$ with differential $d$ satisfying $d^2=0$. Its homology is independent of the chosen regular metric and perturbation up to the declared overall sign and is invariant under isotopy of the based knot data.

items.title: The boundary of a nontrivial knot exterior is incompressible
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth knot that is not ambient isotopic to the standard unknot, let $E_K$ be its chosen compact exterior, and let $T_K=\partial E_K$. There is no properly embedded disk $D\subset E_K$ whose boundary is a simple closed curve in $T_K$ that is not null-homotopic in $T_K$.

items.title: Filtered instanton complex from the cube of knot resolutions
items.statement: Assume full AC. Let $D$ be a finite based diagram of a smooth knot $K\subset S^3$ with ordered crossings $c_1<\cdots<c_n$. The singular instanton resolution complex admits a finite filtration whose first page, with its first differential, is isomorphic to the reduced Khovanov cube of the reflected based diagram $\overline D$. Its spectral sequence converges to $I^\natural(K;\mathbb Z)$. The cube sign at the edge changing $c_j$ is $(-1)^{\sum_{i<j}v_i}$, and the edge operation is multiplication for a merge or comultiplication for a split. Thus its $E_2$ page is the reduced integral Khovanov cohomology of $\overline D$. The claim includes coherent instanton orientations and the unlink group and saddle-map identifications; it asserts no diagram-invariance of intermediate pages.

items.title: Sutured instanton knot homology detects the unknot
items.statement: Assume full AC. For every smooth knot $K\subset S^3$, the rational sutured instanton knot homology $KHI(K;\mathbb Q)$ is finite-dimensional and has dimension at least one; it has dimension one if and only if $K$ is the unknot. Moreover, excision gives an isomorphism $I^\natural(K;\mathbb Q)\cong KHI(K;\mathbb Q)$.

The intermediate pages are not asserted to be knot invariants.
